blue-catfish: Large blue catfish will be in the mix when using cut bait.
Blue catfish are active this week and can be found in the deeper channel waters.
All the tidal rivers in the upper Bay have populations of blue catfish and they can be found in the lower to mid-range sections of the rivers.
largemouth-bass: Water temperatures in the nontidal and tidal waters are still comfortable for largemouth bass, and they are feeling the urge to fatten up for the winter.
Largemouth bass often like to hold near structure waiting for prey to pass by, sort of like the traffic cop waiting behind a billboard sign for a speeding car.
Working whacky rigged soft plastics or craw jigs near the structure is a great way to entice a lurking largemouth bass.
smallmouth-bass: Crayfish are the first choice for smallmouth bass, and they will make a great effort to find them.
It is not uncommon to see the tips of the jaws of smallmouth bass this time of the year showing damaged skin from pinning crayfish to the bottom to snap them up.
The upper Potomac, the Monocacy, Liberty, Prettyboy reservoirs, and Deep Creek Lake are all good places to fish for smallmouth bass.
striped-bass: Upper Chesapeake Bay Fishing is currently good for striped bass, but the weekend does not look too promising.
Anglers are watching water temperatures steadily drop into the mid-50s and lower and striped bass are moving to deeper and warmer waters.
Anglers are drifting cut bait or casting a mix of paddletails and soft plastic jigs in the Conowingo Dam pool for striped bass.
white-perch: Rich Watts sent us this picture from his depth finder of a compact school of white perch that he was fishing on.
Anglers looking for white perch are finding them in about 30 feet of water holding close to the bottom on their depth finders.
Using bottom rigs baited with pieces of bloodworms or lug worms will entice white perch to bite.
